title: Behavior Trees for Robotic Systems: An Empirical Study on Practices and Experiences
abstract: arXiv:2609.22404v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Over the last decade, behavior trees (BT) have become one of the dominant behavior models for coordinating missions of robotic systems. Yet empirical evidence on BT adoption in real-world contexts remains limited, especially regarding practitioners experiences and practices. Without practitioner-grounded evidence from both academic and industrial settings, the research community risks developing guidelines and tools that are plausible in principle but only partly aligned with real challenges. This scarcity of evidence leads to ad-hoc practices, impeding software reuse, maintenance, and evolution. This paper reports a mixed-methods study combining a technical action research investigation at an automotive company with a survey of 34 robotics practitioners. translated_title: 机器人系统中的行为树：关于实践与经验的一项实证研究
translated_abstract: 在过去十年中，行为树（BT）已成为协调机器人系统任务的主导行为模型之一。然而，关于行为树在真实环境中应用的实证证据仍然有限，尤其是关于从业者的经验和实践方面。如果缺乏来自学术界和工业界基于从业者的证据，研究界就可能开发出原则上看似合理、但只能部分契合实际挑战的指南和工具。这种证据的匮乏导致了临时性、随意性的实践，阻碍了软件的重用、维护和演进。本文报告了一项混合方法研究，将在一家汽车公司开展的技术行动研究调查与针对34名机器人从业者的问卷调查相结合。我们的结果表明，行为树改善了团队沟通以及机器人决策逻辑的可理解性，体现了行为树在任务协调之外的实际价值。
tldr: 本文通过将一家汽车公司的技术行动研究与34名机器人从业者的问卷调查相结合的混合方法研究，首次提供了实证证据，表明行为树不仅能协调机器人任务，还能改善团队沟通并提升机器人决策逻辑的可理解性。
en_tdlr: Through a mixed-methods study combining technical action research at an automotive company with a survey of 34 robotics practitioners, this paper provides empirical evidence that behavior trees improve team communication and the understandability of robotic decision-making logic, offering practical value beyond mission coordination.
